newsitem.title: UK: Qatar Air ex-UK cargo revenue rises with capacity.
newsitem.headline: Qatar Air ex-UK cargo revenue rises with capacity.

text.p: Qatar Airways said that 12 to 15 percent of overall UK revenues had been generated from cargo since it started London Heathrow-Doha Airbus A300-600 services on March 31.
UK cargo manager John Curd said this was a considerable improvement from that achieved when smaller Boeing 727s were operated from London Gatwick to Doha in the three preceding years.
"Although the passenger side is our bread-and-butter product, I have tried very hard to increase our cargo yields and am confident of doing better," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"For example, we just missed the deadline to bid for the (UK-Qatar) Royal Mail contract this year but I am looking to secure it in 1998," he said.
From initially four times weekly, on May 25 Heathrow-Doha frequencies were increased to daily, all operated by average 10-tonne cargo capacity passenger A300-600s.
Curd said that from July 1, Qatar Air had commenced its own UK cargo sales, reservations and accounts operation after ceasing to use former UK cargo general sales agent, ANA Aviation Services.
"By the very nature of our previous operation, the GSA tended to sell Doha (because of limited Qatar Air onward connections and capacity)," said Curd.
"Now we are trying hard to sell both Qatar and onward and this policy is starting to work well," he added.
He noted that Qatar Air wide-body A300-600 connections were now available from Doha to Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Bangkok, Colombo, Manila and Khartoum.
"Wee are doing particularly well ex-UK with twice-weekly flights to Manila, a market which is suffering from a capacity shortage at the moment," stated Curd.
"And having appointed Bridges Worldwide as our worldwide courier GSA from June 1, we are expanding our consolidations on twice-weekly services to Bangkok," he said.
He said he was also optimistic about selling ex-Doha onward Qatar Air 727 connections to Dhahran, Jeddah, Kuwait, Muscat and Kathmandu.
